person.description: Who acted, on an approval a person resolved. Absent where nobody acted.

decision-ask-request.description: A question asked before an effect.
decision-ask-request.title: Decision ask request

correlation_source.description: Who chose the bytes of correlation: the boundary that asked, or nobody. The daemon cannot prove a supplied value is an identifier; this marks its provenance.

evaluation_recipe.description: The identifier of the evaluation recipe the decision was taken under; a reader that does not know it reports the record as unverifiable, never evaluates it under other semantics.

principal_references.description: The principal references the evaluation read, sorted and unique: the caller's own reference intersected with the references named by every rule for the asked scope and capability (M3). Recorded so a reader can re-derive the answer without a directory.

delegation.description: Declared by the peer, not verified by the daemon. Every length bound is counted in UTF-8 bytes and published as x-max-bytes; maxLength is the weaker code-point bound a generic validator can check on its own.
delegation.title: Delegation

effect-body.description: The historical reader shape, or the new-writer shape; a body that mixes the two is neither.

oneOf.description: An effect a generation-one writer recorded before the durable decision lifecycle; admitted by the reader, never synthesised into the new shape.

accounting.description: What the count counts: physical records the bytes could not identify, known decisions by identity, or other counted events. Physical and decision counts may describe one failure and are never summed; a historical marker without this member has unknown accounting.

decision_ids.description: The identities of known decisions this marker declares lost, sorted by position and paired one to one with decision_positions; a loss larger than the bound is several markers, never an id-less one.

evidence-entry-writer.description: One immutable entry as a writer of the durable decision lifecycle records it: an effect body carries the decision's reason, rule, digest, correlation and its source, principal references, evaluation recipe and store position. A reader validates against evidence-entry, which also admits the historical shape (article 13).
evidence-entry-writer.title: Evidence entry (new writer)

evidence-export-result.description: A deterministic bounded raw evidence bundle.

manifest_version.description: Which manifest recipe the digest was taken under. A bundle without it predates v3 and is tried against v1 and v2.

content.description: The exact archived bytes, base64 without newlines; the whole administrator policy file, which discloses every rule and reason it holds to every reader admitted to export (A6).

policy_versions.description: One key for every distinct policy version an included effect names, with the bytes or the reason there are none. A missing key is a verification failure, never a successful empty map.

recovery_context.description: Exact entries after the included range, contiguous from its last hash, carried so a verifier can see the closure of the epochs the range represents; supporting context, never additional decision coverage.

evidence-export-result.title: Evidence export result

evidence-page-result.description: A bounded raw range and its verification.
evidence-page-result.title: Evidence page result

evidence-verdict.description: Verification of one range of one scope chain.
evidence-verdict.title: Evidence verdict

grant.description: A decision cached under exact conditions for a bounded lifetime.
grant.title: Grant

grant-signal.description: A heartbeat or terminal change for one issued grant.
grant-signal.title: Grant signal

peer.description: What the kernel recorded for the process that opened the connection.
peer.title: Peer

policy-status.description: The current file authority and its rebuildable materialization.
policy-status.title: Policy status

principal.description: The identity a decision is evaluated against and evidence records.
principal.title: Principal

problem-document.description: A classified refusal or inability to obtain an answer.
problem-document.title: Problem document

status-result.description: The caller-visible state and supported contract generations.

decision_store.description: The decision authority this daemon composed and what its last reconciliation of each scope found; counts and cursors are null, never zero, when it has not run (article 2).

evidence_emission.description: Whether the evidence pipeline is delivering to its store, and what it is holding when it is not. Article 10 makes the pipeline declare its gaps; a store refusing appends holds them where no reader of the chain can see them.

principal.description: The principal as the peer credential established it.

status-result.title: Status result

whoami-result.description: The principal, and the record it was built from, as the daemon saw them.
whoami-result.title: Who am I result

x-stream-hold.description: A boundary that holds this stream keeps the connection's write side open for as long as it holds the grant. The control plane watches the read side for the loss article 10 names, where a peer that closed and a peer that shut its write side down are one event.

servers.description: The host is a placeholder and is ignored by the daemon; the surface is reached over the one Unix domain socket, whose path the deployment configures (see docs/deployment.md).
